leader_humility.name: Leader Humility
leader_humility.description: 3 dimensions: self-awareness, teachability, appreciation of others. Accurate sense of self = integrity + ability. Inflated (dangerous) vs compressed (also bad). TAGS list = decompression. SWOT = deflation. Steve Jobs = tempered narcissist.

self_awareness.name: Self-Awareness
self_awareness.description: Foundation of humility and ethical development. Revisionary ethics = rewriting memory to look better. Forecasting errors = misjudging future behavior. Self-Growth Model: awareness -> reflection -> action -> habit -> character.

commodification.name: Commodification of Society
commodification.description: 5 tests: fairness/equality, coercion/rights, corruption, social value, proper mode of valuation. Market economy vs market society. Dark side of goal setting (Wells Fargo). Pinto case = Ford charged with homicide, overworked recall coordinator.

social_conformity.name: Social Conformity (Asch)
social_conformity.description: Asch studies: people conform even when objectively wrong. More likely to conform with strangers. One dissenting voice breaks the spell. Creates neurological error signal (physically uncomfortable). Sharon Watkins + Cliff Baxter = coalition of two.

role_binding.name: Role Binding (Stanford Prison)
role_binding.description: When assigned a role, brain activates scripts that can override moral identity. Zimbardo prison experiment. Milgram: obedience + responsibility vacuum + incremental escalation. We ALWAYS have a choice.

moral_courage.name: Moral Courage
moral_courage.description: Requires 3 things: commitment to moral principles + risk present + willingness to endure. Usually long process not one moment. Direct dissent = state clearly wrong. Indirect dissent = ask for info, frame around org values, seek alternatives.

ethics_movies.name: Ethics Movie Case
ethics_movies.description: 3 films: A Man for All Seasons (sustained courage, indirect dissent), 13 Lives (weighing principles when rules fail), Quiz Show (repeated temptation erodes resolve, rationalization, weak actor takes fall).

giving_voice_to_values.name: Giving Voice to Values
giving_voice_to_values.description: 4 voice strengths: metaphors/stories, building coalitions, pragmatism, logic/reason. 4 dilemma types: justice vs mercy, utilitarian vs deontology, long vs short term, honesty vs loyalty. Diplomat/team player posture beats crusader.

byu_workplace.name: BYU Grads in the Workplace
byu_workplace.description: Build relational capital BEFORE needing it. Ammon model: serve first, build trust. Happy hour: show up for first one (primacy effect). Fairness for All: protect both religious liberty AND LGBTQ rights. Great clarity in principles, great charity in practice.

stakeholder_theory.name: Stakeholder Theory
stakeholder_theory.description: HIGHEST PRIORITY TOPIC. Salience model: Power + Legitimacy + Urgency. All 3 = Definitive (top priority). P+L = Dominant. L+U = Dependent. P+U = Dangerous. None = Non-stakeholder. Friedman counter: just maximize shareholder value. Pros: long-term thinking, CSR. Cons: slower decisions, performative CSR risk.

conflict_of_interest.name: Conflict of Interest
conflict_of_interest.description: ALWAYS DISCLOSE. Then withdraw if necessary. When another role compromises your objectivity as an organizational decision-maker. Nepotism = family role vs manager role. Two steps: 1) disclose 2) withdraw.

diversity_affirmative_action.name: Diversity and Affirmative Action
diversity_affirmative_action.description: NOT the same thing. Affirmative action is NOT unconstitutional (false). Education: race-based numeric factors banned, case-by-case OK. Employment: still legal except CA, MI, WA. Requirements: written, proves disparity, temporary. Human capital decisions = highest lawsuit risk.

crucial_conversations.name: Ethics Academy Awards / Crucial Conversations
crucial_conversations.description: Moral muteness = staying silent. Moral superiority = acting holier-than-thou. Both fail. Prepare in advance: identify conflicting principles, find creative third alternative, frame around org values, use your voice strengths.

ethical_frameworks.name: The 4 Ethical Frameworks
ethical_frameworks.description: Virtue ethics: what kind of person does this make me? Utilitarianism: greatest good for greatest number. Deontology: rule-based duty regardless of outcome. Social contract: what would rational people agree to? Know all 4.

kohlberg.name: Kohlberg's Moral Development
kohlberg.description: 3 levels: Pre-Conventional (avoid punishment/seek reward), Conventional (rules/social norms), Post-Conventional (principles/universal ethics). Goal: operate at stage 5-6.

moral_regulation.name: Moral Regulation
moral_regulation.description: Moral licensing: past good behavior creates permission to slip. Moral cleansing: doing good to offset wrong. Prescriptive = proactively do good. Proscriptive = avoid doing wrong. Aim for prescriptive.

moral_rationalization.name: Moral Rationalization
moral_rationalization.description: Tactics: denial of responsibility, denial of injury, appeal to higher loyalties, condemnation of condemners, displacement of responsibility. Know counters to each. Quiz Show = rationalization dressed as idealism.

csr.name: Corporate Social Responsibility
csr.description: Companies taking responsibility beyond legal requirements. Stakeholder theory leads to CSR. Genuine CSR = strong business case. Performative CSR backfires. Friedman argument: return dividends and let shareholders choose charities.

hedonic_eudemonic.name: Hedonic vs Eudemonic Happiness
hedonic_eudemonic.description: Hedonic = pleasure/novelty-oriented (life as a carnival). Eudemonic = virtue/growth-oriented (life as a university or weight room). Eudemonic produces deeper lasting wellbeing. Connected to Adam II (roots/character) vs Adam I (branches/accomplishment).

moral_relativism.name: Moral Relativism (Koukl's Critique)
moral_relativism.description: Koukl's two key flaws: (1) relativists cannot logically evaluate others' moral actions, (2) relativists cannot consistently make claims about good or evil. Internal contradiction: they want to say tolerance is good but their framework forbids universal moral claims.

company_ethics_levels.name: Company Ethics Levels (A-F Framework)
company_ethics_levels.description: Tiered framework for evaluating company ethical behavior. A = exceptional, proactive ethics. B = above average, good practices. C = meets minimum standards/advertised guarantee. D = below standard. F = actively harmful. Sam's jacket company went from B (high quality, customer-focused) to C (meets only the minimum guarantee).
